nodes.description: The M-motif normally makes a dynamic, regulated contact with myosin S2 and actin. Mutant sMyBP-C binds myosin abnormally tightly (or weakly), and the LKR duplication inhibits myosin ATPase activity and actin sliding in vitro, disturbing cross-bridge cycling.

evidence.reference_title: From bedside to bench: A multimodal approach uncovering the molecular basis of the MYBPC1-linked Myotrem myopathy.
evidence.snippet: We show that the LKR-duplication stabilizes local helicity but alters global domain dynamics, leading to increased myosin binding, while impairing myosin-ATPase activity and crossbridge cycling.

evidence.reference_title: Sarcomeric deficits underlie MYBPC1-associated myopathy with myogenic tremor.
evidence.snippet: In adulthood, clinical findings include axial muscle weakness; proximal appendicular weakness; scoliosis with thoracic/sternal deformity; rigidity of the spine; contractures in the elbows, arms, and/or feet; and high-frequency tremor (~10 Hz) of irregular amplitude that is accentuated by posture and/or activity and is more noticeable in the hands than the legs

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in MYBPC1 are associated with myogenic tremor and mild myopathy.
evidence.snippet: The patient had hypotonia and a postural hand tremor since infancy, followed by a delay in gross motor milestone acquisition, with independent walking achieved at 2 years of age.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital tremor and myopathy secondary to novel MYBPC1 variant.
evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a family with three generations of variably affected members exhibiting a novel variant in MYBPC1 (c.656 T > C, p.Leu219Pro).

nodes.description: Disease variants (p.Tyr247His, p.Glu248Lys, p.Leu259Pro, p.Leu263Arg, p.Leu219Pro and an in-frame p.Leu266_Arg268dup) cluster in or near the NH2-terminal M-motif of sMyBP-C, the region that binds myosin S2. Y247H, E248K and the LKR duplication increase M-motif binding to myosin, whereas L263R decreases it, so the variants are not simple loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in MYBPC1 are associated with myogenic tremor and mild myopathy.
evidence.snippet: The Y247H and E248K mutations are located in the NH2 -terminal M-motif of sMyBP-C.

nodes.description: Heterozygous mice are smaller, weak and tremulous from the neonatal period, with tremor that lessens in adulthood and appears with posture or intention, as in patients; homozygotes die shortly after birth with severe tremor and respiratory failure. Aged mice show muscle- and sex-specific decline.
EMG shows a myopathic pattern without spontaneous activity, with normal nerve conduction. This supports a muscle rather than nerve origin of the weakness.

nodes.description: A subset of slow type 1 E248K fibers show spontaneous, rhythmic sarcomere oscillations during submaximal calcium activation, and fast fibers show raised stretch activation. Normal sMyBP-C is proposed to damp this oscillatory activity, and its loss of control is proposed to start the tremor in muscle. Patient tremor physiology suggests a central loop then amplifies it. The tremor mechanism is a working model, shown only in mouse fibers.
